narrative.overview:
billsend is a local-first invoice generator: no accounts, no servers, no tracking, all data in the browser's IndexedDB. The interface should feel like a precise, trustworthy document tool, closer to a spreadsheet or a design canvas than to a consumer landing page. The invoice being edited is the loudest thing on screen: a sheet of white A4 paper lying on a grey desk, surrounded by quiet chrome.

The visual language is deliberately quiet around that sheet. Chrome is achromatic, the brand accent is a single blue-violet ramp, radii are small, and controls are compact. The paper itself never changes with the app theme, because it is a preview of the PDF that gets downloaded.

The marketing homepage is the one place the system changes world. It is a security-printed document, presenting billsend's privacy the way a banknote presents its anti-forgery features: a pale mint safety-paper tint under a fine guilloche underprint, intaglio ink in billsend blue, engraved wide capitals in Archivo, numbering-machine red kept for serials and live counters, and perforations and microprint as its dividers. Invoices are white paper slips lying on that tint, and the privacy proof (the browser's own count of requests to other websites) is printed on a slip's counterfoil. Its motion is one authored moment on load: the headline rises, the slip lands, and the corner rosette engraves itself.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral chrome; colour is reserved for the brand accent and for status.
One accent: the blue-violet `brand` ramp carries every emphasis.
White paper on a grey desk: the invoice page previews the PDF exactly.
Tight geometry: 3px surfaces, 4px controls, 32px default control height.
Security-print homepage: tinted ground, generated guilloche, engraved Archivo capitals, red serials, perforated dividers, one engraved plate CTA.
Light only in practice: `.dark` tokens exist but nothing enables them yet.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The blue-violet `brand` ramp is the only accent. Never introduce a second hue for emphasis; status colours are for status only. The homepage's numbering red is a printing ink, not an accent, and lives under the Numbering Red Rule.

rules.name: The 600 Fill Rule
rules.body: Solid brand fills under white text are `brand-600` or darker. `brand-500` is for rings and borders.

rules.name: The Paper Rule
rules.body: The invoice page is white paper with dark ink in every app theme, because it previews the printed PDF. Anything drawn on the page uses `paper-*` tokens (or the brand wash for edit affordances), never chrome roles or raw Tailwind greys or blues.

rules.name: The Numbering Red Rule
rules.body: `numbering` prints serials and live counts and nothing else: never a link, a heading, an error, or emphasis. It is always set in the numbering face.

rules.name: The Security Ink Rule
rules.body: The homepage takes its colour from the security-print tokens, white paper, and the brand ramp; it uses no raw Tailwind greys, and the editor never uses the security-print tokens.

rules.name: The Dark Mode Honesty Rule
rules.body: `.dark` values exist for every chrome role, but no route sets the `dark` class today. Use role tokens so dark mode stays possible; do not claim or test light/dark parity until something enables it.

rules.name: The Engraved Recipe Rule
rules.body: Every homepage Archivo element is built from the route's shared recipes (`ENGRAVED`, `NUMBERING`, `FORM_LABEL`, `HEADLINE`) and adds only size, leading, and colour.

rules.name: The Reading Is Geist Rule
rules.body: Archivo sets headings, labels, plates, numerals, and microprint. Every sentence a visitor reads (leads, check descriptions, notes, answers, captions) stays in Geist.

rules.name: The Archivo Stays Home Rule
rules.body: Archivo is imported and preloaded only by the homepage route and appears only there. The editor and dialogs never use it.

rules.name: The Perforation Rule
rules.body: On the homepage, rows and regions divide with a 2px dashed perforation (`perforation` on the tint and slips, `brand-400` at 50% on the band) or a microprint rule. Solid hairlines are reserved for outlining an object (the document, a slip, a bar) and for the rows inside an example invoice.

rules.name: The Float-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this is above the page". In-flow cards, rows, and panels get a hairline, not a shadow.

rules.name: The Slip Rule
rules.body: On the homepage, lifted surfaces are white paper slips lying on the tint: white, `ink` at 15% hairline, `rounded-surface`, `shadow-floating`, upright. The hero document, the tour notes, and the privacy band are printed on the ground and sit flat.

dos: Do reference semantic roles (`bg-background`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`) in app chrome so retheming stays possible.
Do use `paper-*` tokens for everything drawn on the invoice page, and `brand-50` plus `brand-500` for its edit affordances.
Do put solid brand fills on `brand-600` (hover `brand-700`) and keep `brand-500` for focus rings and borders.
Do keep the A4 page free of responsive breakpoints; scale it with zoom.
Do give coarse pointers 44px targets with `pointer-coarse:` variants.
Do separate stacked and adjacent surfaces with `flex` or `grid` plus `gap-*` (use `gap-px` on a coloured parent for hairlines).
Do stay on `rounded-surface` / `rounded-control` and the 32px control height for chrome.
Do reach for `shadow-menu` for floating chrome rather than picking raw shadow utilities per component.
Do tint destructive actions; reserve solid saturated fills for the brand.
Do mirror any new PDF colour as a literal hex in the renderer and record it in the PDF palette here.
Do use the one `CreateInvoiceLink` engraved plate for every homepage primary action, with the same label everywhere and one on screen at a time.
Do build homepage Archivo text from the shared `ENGRAVED`, `NUMBERING`, `FORM_LABEL`, and `HEADLINE` recipes, and keep reading text in Geist.
Do divide homepage rows and regions with 2px dashed perforations or microprint rules.
Do generate any new guilloche from `utils/guilloche.ts` parameters and colour it with `currentColor` set from the `guilloche` token.
Do keep homepage motion in plain CSS that plays without JavaScript and degrades to fades under reduced motion.
Do give JavaScript-only homepage content a same-height plain stand-in until hydration, and prefer native elements (`<details>`) that need none.
Do prove privacy claims with something the visitor can see or check (the live counter, plain checks) rather than decorative ticks.
Do list homepage colour transitions by property (`color`, `background-color`, `text-decoration-color`) so focus outlines never fade.
donts: Don't use `space-y-*`, `space-x-*`, `divide-x`, or `divide-y` (breaks with conditional and fragment children; owner-controlled `gap` is the rule).
Don't put white text on `brand-500`; it fails AA.
Don't let the invoice page follow the app theme or use chrome roles, raw `zinc-*`/`blue-*`, or responsive classes.
Don't hard-code hex or raw `neutral-*` greys in app chrome or on the homepage; hex belongs to the PDF renderer.
Don't introduce a second accent hue; numbering red prints serials and live counts only.
Don't use Archivo or the security-print tokens outside the homepage.
Don't let microprint carry information; it is a rule, hidden from assistive tech.
Don't use `transition-colors` on focusable homepage elements; it animates `outline-color`.
Don't reach for heavy or black shadows; prefer a hairline border, and keep any shadow soft and neutral.
